summary.en: Israel has intensified its operations in southern Lebanon, striking Qantara, conducting overflights that wounded a Lebanese footballer, and detonating a large explosion in Khiam while drones flew over Beirut. The Lebanese army seized a large quantity of weapons in a Beirut suburb warehouse and reported another arms depot capture in the city’s southern suburbs. Hezbollah arrested five members in Batroun, continued artillery fire on Israeli positions, and began cash payments to war victims and displaced families. UNRWA funding cuts have deepened hardship for Palestinian refugees in Lebanon. 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Israel har økt operasjonene i Sør-Libanon, rammet Qantara, gjennomført overflyvninger som såret en libanesisk fotballspiller, og detonert en stor eksplosjon i Khiam mens droner fløy over Beirut. Den libanesiske hæren beslagla en stor mengde våpen i et lager i en forstad til Beirut og rapporterte om et nytt våpenlager som ble tatt i byens sørlige forsteder. Hizbollah arresterte fem medlemmer i Batroun, fortsatte artilleriskudd mot israelske posisjoner, og begynte å betale kontant til krigsofre og fordrevne familier. Kutt i UNRWA-finansieringen har forverret situasjonen for palestinske flyktninger i Libanon. 4 335 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
